ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown, student Xiao Zhang holds the teacher's isosceles right-angled triangle ruler, placing it between two stacks of rectangular solid teaching aids, with $\angle ACB=90^\circ$ and $AC=BC$. If the height of each rectangular solid teaching aid is $6\text{cm}$, what is the length of the distance $DE$ in $\text{cm}$ between the two stacks of rectangular solid teaching aids?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the given, we have: $AC=BC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AD\perp DE$, $BE\perp DE$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADC=\angle CEB=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore \angle ACD+\angle BCE=90^\circ$, $\angle ACD+\angle DAC=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BCE=\angle DAC$,\\
In $\triangle ADC$ and $\triangle CEB$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle ADC=\angle CEB \\
\angle DAC=\angle BCE \\
AC=BC
\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ADC\cong \triangle CEB$ (AAS),\\
$\therefore CD=BE$, $AD=CE$,\\
$\because DE=CD+CE$,\\
$\therefore DE=BE+AD$,\\
$\because$ the thickness of a rectangular solid teaching aid is $6\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore AD=24\text{cm}$, $BE=18\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore$ the distance $DE$ between the two stacks of rectangular solid teaching aids is $24+18=\boxed{42}\text{cm}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown, student Xiao Zhang holds the teacher's isosceles right-angled triangle ruler, placing it between two stacks of rectangular solid teaching aids, with $\angle ACB=90^\circ$ and $AC=BC$. If the height of each rectangular solid teaching aid is $6\text{cm}$, what is the length of the distance $DE$ in $\text{cm}$ between the two stacks of rectangular solid teaching aids?
raw_record.answer:
Solution: From the given, we have: $AC=BC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AD\perp DE$, $BE\perp DE$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADC=\angle CEB=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore \angle ACD+\angle BCE=90^\circ$, $\angle ACD+\angle DAC=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BCE=\angle DAC$,\\
In $\triangle ADC$ and $\triangle CEB$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle ADC=\angle CEB \\
\angle DAC=\angle BCE \\
AC=BC
\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ADC\cong \triangle CEB$ (AAS),\\
$\therefore CD=BE$, $AD=CE$,\\
$\because DE=CD+CE$,\\
$\therefore DE=BE+AD$,\\
$\because$ the thickness of a rectangular solid teaching aid is $6\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore AD=24\text{cm}$, $BE=18\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore$ the distance $DE$ between the two stacks of rectangular solid teaching aids is $24+18=\boxed{42}\text{cm}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the triangular ruler is clamped between two stacks of rectangular prism teaching aids, point A is at the top of the teaching aids on the left side, and point D is directly below A; point B is at the top of the teaching aids on the right side, and point E is directly below B; D, C, and E are on the same horizontal line. There are 4 pieces of teaching aids on the left side, and 3 pieces of teaching aids on the right side. The height of each piece of teaching aid is 6 cm, so AD = 4 × 6 = 24 cm, BE = 3 × 6 = 18 cm.
Reasoning: It is known that triangle ABC is an isosceles right triangle, AC = BC, ∠ACB = 90°. Because AD and BE are both perpendicular to the horizontal line DE, ∠ADC = ∠CEB = 90°, and triangle ADC and triangle CEB are both right triangles. Also because D, C, and E are collinear and ∠ACB = 90°, ∠ACD + ∠BCE = 90°; in right triangle ADC, ∠ACD + ∠CAD = 90°, therefore ∠BCE = ∠CAD. Thus, in triangle ADC and triangle CEB, there are ∠ADC = ∠CEB, ∠CAD = ∠BCE, and AC = BC, so the two triangles are congruent. From congruence, CD = BE and CE = AD can be obtained. Therefore DE = CD + CE = BE + AD = 18 + 24 = 42 cm.
